```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_canagliflozin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_canagliflozin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70644> (open access, with Supporting
  information)

The paper extrapolates two adult canagliflozin models to paediatric patients
aged 10-17 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM): the adult population PK
model (Hoeben 2016) and the adult HbA1c PK/PD model (de Winter 2017). The PK
model was updated by removing the adult covariates that did not extrapolate
(age, eGFR, BMI) and re-estimating only the residual error; the PK/PD model was
fitted sequentially on the individual PK parameters, with the baseline HbA1c,
the placebo effect and the residual error re-estimated and covariates for
background insulin and randomised arm added. Both stages are packaged in one
model file so that a canagliflozin dose drives the HbA1c response directly.

# Population

The PK analysis used 330 canagliflozin concentrations from 90 paediatric
patients: 17 from an open-label phase 1 study (100 or 300 mg once daily for 14
days, intensive sampling on day 14) and 73 from the canagliflozin arm of a
randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 study (100 mg once daily, 12 patients
uptitrated to 300 mg at week 13; trough samples at weeks 12, 26 and 52). Median
age was 15 years (10-17), median body weight 79.5 kg (44.8-170), 67.8% were
female, and the cohort was 33.3% Asian, 22.2% White Hispanic, 20.0% Black and
16.7% White non-Hispanic (Table 1). The PK/PD analysis used 702 HbA1c values
from 160 phase 3 patients (73 canagliflozin, 87 placebo); 40% were on background
insulin with or without metformin (Table S1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_canagliflozin")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. They are
collected here for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc_male` (Vc/F, males, 75.8 kg) | log(99.3) L, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lvc_female` (Vc/F, females, 75.8 kg) | log(82.6) L, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lkel` (ke at 100 mg/day) | log(0.145) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lka` | log(3.68) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lk12` (k23, central to peripheral) | log(0.101) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lk21` (k32, peripheral to central) | log(0.0856) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `ltlag_nonencap` / `ltlag_overencap` | log(0.147) / log(0.262) h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `ld1` (zero-order input duration) | log(0.604) h, fixed | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.583, fixed; reference 75.8 kg | Table 2 and footnote b |
| `e_dose_cana_mgd_kel` | -0.0631, fixed; reference 100 mg | Table 2 and footnote c |
| `etalvc`, `etalkel`, `etalka`, `etalk21`, `etaltlag` | 14.6, 23.1, 188, 36.2, 93.6 CV%, fixed | Table 2 (omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)) |
| `expSdPhase1` / `expSdPhase3` | 0.227 / 1.14 | Table 2 |
| `lrbase_ins_pbo`, `lrbase_ins_cana`, `lrbase_noins_pbo`, `lrbase_noins_cana` | log(8.50), log(7.82), log(7.91), log(7.22) % | Table 4 |
| `lkout` | log(log(2)/28.2) 1/day, fixed | Table 4 and footnote a |
| `pbo_ins` / `pbo_noins` (Efp) | 0.171 / -0.238 % | Table 4 |
| `emax` | -0.738 %, fixed | Table 4 |
| `lec50` | 4.12 log ng/mL, fixed (EC50 61.6 ng/mL) | Table 4 and footnote b |
| `etalrbase` / `etapbo` | variance 0.011 (lognormal) / 0.369 (normal), fixed | Table 4; Methods |
| `expSd_Hba1c` | 0.0773 | Table 4 |
| Two-compartment PK in rate constants, lag then zero-order input into the depot, first-order absorption | n/a | Methods 'popPK and PK/PD models' |
| Additive residual error on log-transformed concentrations, separate rich / sparse variances | n/a | Methods 'popPK and PK/PD models' |
| `d/dt(Hba1c) = Ef + kin - kout * Hba1c` | n/a | Supplement Equation 1 |
| `Ef = kout * (Efc + Efp) * (H(0) - 5) / (8 - 5)` | n/a | Supplement Equation 2 |
| `Efc = Emax * C / (C + EC50)` | n/a | Supplement Equation 3 |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. The cohort below approximates the
paediatric population: body weight is drawn log-normally around the Table 1
median of 79.5 kg and truncated to the observed 44.8-170 kg range, the same
for both sexes because the paper does not report weight by sex. As in the
paper's Table S2, exposures are summarised separately for males and females, so
each regimen gets 100 males and 100 females (200 per regimen). All patients take
overencapsulated tablets, the formulation used in the paediatric studies.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261118)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261118)

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~dose, ~tau, ~tdd,
  "100 mg QD",  100,   24,   100,
  "50 mg BID",  50,    12,   100,
  "300 mg QD",  300,   24,   300,
  "150 mg BID", 150,   12,   300
)

n_per_sex <- 100L
draw_weight <- function(n) {
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(79.5), 0.30))
  pmin(pmax(wt, 44.8), 170)
}
pk_subjects <- tibble(
  sub = seq_len(2L * n_per_sex),
  SEXF = rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n_per_sex),
  WT = draw_weight(2L * n_per_sex)
)

make_pk_events <- function(reg, id_offset) {
  subj <- pk_subjects |>
    mutate(
      id = id_offset + sub,
      regimen = reg$regimen,
      DOSE_CANA_MGD = reg$tdd,
      FORM_CANAGLIFLOZIN_OVERENCAP = 1L,
      STUDY_PHASE3 = 0L,
      CONMED_INSULIN = 0L,
      TRT_CANAGLIFLOZIN = 1L
    )
  dose_times <- seq(0, 168 - reg$tau, by = reg$tau)
  obs_times <- seq(144, 168, by = 0.25)
  # The model has two endpoints (Cc, then Hba1c); dvid = 1 points the
  # concentration observations at the Cc endpoint.
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = reg$dose, rate = -2, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

pk_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_pk_events(regimens[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * 1000L)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(pk_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

Seven days of dosing reach steady state (the terminal half-life is about half a
day). Exposure is summarised from the individual predictions, which include the
inter-individual variability; see the deviations section for the residual
error.

```{r simulate-pk}
mod <- readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_canagliflozin")
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = pk_events,
  keep = c("regimen", "SEXF"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(
    sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)
  )
```

## Steady-state profiles (Figure S7)

```{r figure-s7}
sim_pk |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10),
    Q50 = median(Cc),
    Q90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 144, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the first day-7 dose (h)",
    y = "Canagliflozin (ng/mL)",
    title = "Steady-state canagliflozin profiles, paediatric T2DM",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles. Replicates the paediatric panels of Figure S7 of Goeyvaerts 2026."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state AUC24h and Cmax are computed over the last 24 h of the 7-day
regimen (two 12-h dosing intervals for BID, so AUC24h covers the whole daily
dose, as in the paper).

Two versions are computed: from the individual predictions `Cc`, and from the
same profiles with the phase 1 residual error (log-scale SD 0.227) applied to
every 0.25-h sample (`sim`), because the paper's simulated profiles included
residual error.

```{r pknca}
dose_df <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(regimen, ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"), sep = " | ")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

run_nca <- function(conc_df, dose_df) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

sim_nca <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(regimen, sex, sep = " | ")) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, sim, treatment)

nca_res <- run_nca(select(sim_nca, -sim), dose_df)
nca_res_ruv <- run_nca(sim_nca |> mutate(Cc = sim) |> select(-sim), dose_df)

cmax_ruv <- as.data.frame(nca_res_ruv$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(cmax_ruv = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

nca_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  separate(treatment, into = c("regimen", "sex"), sep = " \\| ", remove = FALSE) |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
```

## Simulated exposure by regimen and sex (Figure 2)

```{r figure-2}
nca_ind |>
  pivot_longer(c(auclast, cmax), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, auclast = "AUC24h,ss (h*ng/mL)", cmax = "Cmax,ss (ng/mL)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(regimen, value, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Paediatric panels of Figure 2 of Goeyvaerts 2026."
  )
```

## Comparison against published simulated exposure (Table S2)

Table S2 reports the mean of the simulated steady-state AUC24h and Cmax per
regimen and sex, so the simulated values are summarised by their mean as well.

```{r nca-compare}
published_s2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,            ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "100 mg QD | Male",    6682,     1052,
  "100 mg QD | Female",  8872,     1399,
  "50 mg BID | Male",    6655,     695,
  "50 mg BID | Female",  8866,     922,
  "300 mg QD | Male",    21472,    3237,
  "300 mg QD | Female",  28509,    4306,
  "150 mg BID | Male",   21382,    2171,
  "150 mg BID | Female", 28487,    2882
)

sim_mean <- nca_ind |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(auclast = mean(auclast), cmax = mean(cmax), .groups = "drop")

# Rows labelled 'with residual error' compare the Cmax of the noisy profiles
# against the same published value.
sim_cmp <- bind_rows(
  sim_mean,
  cmax_ruv |>
    transmute(treatment = paste(treatment, "| with residual error"), cmax = cmax_ruv)
)
ref_cmp <- bind_rows(
  published_s2,
  published_s2 |>
    transmute(treatment = paste(treatment, "| with residual error"), cmax)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp,
  reference = ref_cmp,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "h*ng/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
# The residual-error rows carry Cmax only.
cmp <- cmp[!(grepl("with residual error", cmp$treatment) & !grepl("^Cmax", cmp[[1]])), ]
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Mean simulated steady-state AUC24h (AUC over the last 24 h) and Cmax versus Goeyvaerts 2026 Table S2 (paediatric). * differs by >20%."
)

chk_pk <- sim_mean |>
  inner_join(published_s2, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub")) |>
  mutate(auc_pct = 100 * (auclast_sim / auclast_pub - 1))
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed volume, rate constant, dose effect or unit factor moves
  # every mean AUC by far more than this; the residual difference is weight
  # sampling and Monte-Carlo error of 100 subjects per cell.
  abs(median(chk_pk$auc_pct)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(chk_pk$auc_pct), 0.9) < 20
)
```

AUC24h agrees with Table S2 in every cell. The Cmax of the individual
predictions is about 20-30% below Table S2, while the Cmax of the profiles with
residual error is close to it. The typical male of 80 kg already has a
steady-state Cmax of about 890 ng/mL at 100 mg QD, against a published mean of
1052 ng/mL, so the gap is not a cohort effect: Table S2 most likely reports the
maximum of simulated profiles that carry residual error, which raises the mean
maximum and compresses the QD-to-BID ratio (about 1.5 in Table S2 against about
1.6-1.7 for the predictions). The size of that inflation depends on the
simulated sampling times, which the paper does not give, so Cmax is reported
here but not used as a pass/fail check.

The individual steady-state AUC24h estimated by the authors for the observed
paediatric patients (Table 3) is of the same size: mean 6574 (males) and 8397
(females) h*ng/mL at 100 mg QD, 22 480 and 29 930 h*ng/mL at 300 mg QD.

# HbA1c

## Analytic steady state of the turnover equations

With a constant canagliflozin concentration `C`, Supplement Equations 1-3 give
the steady state `H_ss = H(0) + (Efc + Efp) * (H(0) - 5) / 3`. A placebo subject
(no drug) without background insulin, on the canagliflozin-arm baseline,
should therefore settle at `7.22 - 0.238 * (7.22 - 5) / 3 = 7.044` %.

```{r analytic}
mod_typ <- mod |> rxode2::zeroRe()
ev_ss <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 24 * 7 * 52), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "Hba1c",
  WT = 75.8, SEXF = 0L, DOSE_CANA_MGD = 0, FORM_CANAGLIFLOZIN_OVERENCAP = 1L,
  STUDY_PHASE3 = 0L, CONMED_INSULIN = 0L, TRT_CANAGLIFLOZIN = 1L
)
ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_ss, returnType = "data.frame",
                      atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)
h_ss_expected <- 7.22 - 0.238 * (7.22 - 5) / 3
stopifnot(abs(ss$Hba1c[1] - 7.22) < 1e-6, abs(ss$Hba1c[2] - h_ss_expected) < 1e-4)
c(simulated = ss$Hba1c[2], analytic = h_ss_expected)
```

## Simulated HbA1c over 26 weeks (Figure 4, Table S3)

The paper simulated HbA1c for the four regimens using covariates sampled
jointly from the PK/PD data set, which pools the canagliflozin and placebo
arms; the randomised arm enters only through the baseline HbA1c. The cohort
below draws the arm (73/160 canagliflozin), background insulin within arm
(27/73 and 37/87, Table S1), sex (68.1% female) and weight, and gives every
subject the simulated canagliflozin regimen. Its expected typical baseline is
`(27 * 7.82 + 46 * 7.22 + 37 * 8.50 + 50 * 7.91) / 160 = 7.83` %, the mean at
week 0 of Figure 4A, which supports this reading of the paper's covariate
sampling.

```{r cohort-pd}
n_pd <- 200L
trt <- rbinom(n_pd, 1, 73 / 160)
pd_subjects <- tibble(
  sub = seq_len(n_pd),
  TRT_CANAGLIFLOZIN = trt,
  CONMED_INSULIN = rbinom(n_pd, 1, ifelse(trt == 1, 27 / 73, 37 / 87)),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_pd, 1, 109 / 160),
  WT = draw_weight(n_pd)
)

make_pd_events <- function(reg, id_offset) {
  subj <- pd_subjects |>
    mutate(
      id = id_offset + sub,
      regimen = reg$regimen,
      DOSE_CANA_MGD = reg$tdd,
      FORM_CANAGLIFLOZIN_OVERENCAP = 1L,
      STUDY_PHASE3 = 1L
    )
  end_h <- 26 * 7 * 24
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = seq(0, end_h - reg$tau, by = reg$tau)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = reg$dose, rate = -2, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = seq(0, end_h, by = 2 * 7 * 24)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "Hba1c")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

pd_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_pd_events(regimens[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * 1000L)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(pd_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r simulate-pd}
sim_pd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = pd_events,
  keep = c("regimen"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(time %% (2 * 7 * 24) == 0) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(cfb = Hba1c - Hba1c[time == 0]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    week = time / (7 * 24),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen),
    tdd = ifelse(regimen %in% c("100 mg QD", "50 mg BID"), "Total daily dose 100 mg", "Total daily dose 300 mg")
  )
```

```{r figure-4}
sim_pd |>
  pivot_longer(c(Hba1c, cfb), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, Hba1c = "HbA1c (%)", cfb = "Change from baseline HbA1c (%)")) |>
  group_by(tdd, regimen, metric, week) |>
  summarise(m = mean(value), s = sd(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(week, m, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - s, ymax = m + s), width = 0.4,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ tdd, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "Mean +/- SD of individual predictions. Replicates Figure 4 of Goeyvaerts 2026."
  )
```

```{r table-s3}
published_s3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~hba1c_pub, ~cfb_pub,
  "100 mg QD",  7.23,       -0.597,
  "50 mg BID",  7.21,       -0.621,
  "300 mg QD",  7.14,       -0.693,
  "150 mg BID", 7.13,       -0.704
)
wk26 <- sim_pd |>
  filter(week == 26) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    hba1c_sim = mean(Hba1c), hba1c_sd = sd(Hba1c),
    cfb_sim = mean(cfb), cfb_sd = sd(cfb),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  inner_join(published_s3, by = "regimen")

wk26 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "HbA1c wk 26, simulated mean (%)" = hba1c_sim,
    "HbA1c SD" = hba1c_sd,
    "HbA1c wk 26, Table S3 (%)" = hba1c_pub,
    "Change from baseline, simulated mean (%)" = cfb_sim,
    "Change SD" = cfb_sd,
    "Change from baseline, Table S3 (%)" = cfb_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-26 HbA1c and change from baseline versus Goeyvaerts 2026 Table S3.")

stopifnot(
  # Each mean is over 200 subjects; Monte-Carlo SE is about 0.07 for HbA1c and
  # 0.045 for the change from baseline. A wrong Emax, EC50, half-life or the
  # (H(0) - 5)/3 scaling moves the change by 0.2-0.7 percentage points.
  all(abs(wk26$cfb_sim - wk26$cfb_pub) < 0.2),
  all(abs(wk26$hba1c_sim - wk26$hba1c_pub) < 0.35)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Weight and sex.** Body weight is drawn log-normally (median 79.5 kg,
  log-SD 0.30, truncated to 44.8-170 kg) for both sexes; the paper samples
  observed covariate vectors, which are not public, and does not report weight
  by sex.
- **Residual error in the exposure and HbA1c summaries.** The paper says its
  simulated profiles included residual error but does not say which of the two
  PK residual SDs, nor the simulated sampling times. AUC24h is compared on the
  individual predictions (residual error barely changes a mean AUC). For Cmax,
  the individual predictions fall 20-30% below Table S2 while profiles with the
  phase 1 residual SD (0.227) on a 0.25-h grid land within 8% of it; the
  sparse-data SD of 1.14 would give far larger Cmax spreads than the roughly
  33% CV of Table S2. Cmax is therefore shown both ways and not used as a
  pass/fail check. The HbA1c summaries use individual predictions: the spread
  of Figure 4A at week 0 matches the baseline variability without the HbA1c
  residual error.
- **One file for both stages.** The authors fitted the popPK and the PK/PD
  model sequentially (the PK/PD fit used the individual PK estimates). Both are
  packaged as a single model so that a dose drives HbA1c; the PK stage is
  unchanged when only `Cc` is of interest.
- **Baseline HbA1c strata.** Table 4 reports one baseline per combination of
  background insulin and randomised arm. They are encoded as four parameters
  selected by `CONMED_INSULIN` and `TRT_CANAGLIFLOZIN` rather than as a
  reference plus covariate effects, so that the printed values are reproduced
  exactly. The arm term captures a baseline imbalance between the randomised
  groups, not a drug effect.
- **Placebo subjects and the dose covariate.** The total-daily-dose effect on ke
  is a power of `DOSE_CANA_MGD / 100`; for a subject who receives no
  canagliflozin (`DOSE_CANA_MGD = 0`) the model uses the 100 mg reference so
  that ke stays finite. This has no effect on any prediction because no drug is
  present.
- **Residual-error strata.** `STUDY_PHASE3` selects the log-scale residual SD
  for the canagliflozin concentration (0 = phase 1 rich data, 1 = the sparse
  'Phase 2 and 3' stratum of Table 2). The paediatric sparse data came from the
  phase 3 study only.
- **Placebo effect onset.** Supplement Equation 2 applies the placebo effect Efp
  from the start of treatment; the model does the same (t = 0 is the first
  dose).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for the article as of 2026-11-18.
